tier_reason: Upgraded C to A on the LangArena precedent (Etc::Words, Template::Parse, Distance::NGram entries in this wave): public code for every side (v/fannkuchredux.v, c/src/fannkuchredux.c, cpp/src/fannkuchredux.cpp; workload n=8, 700 iterations, checksum in run.js), C/C++ flags in c/Makefile and cpp/Makefile, the V build command, compiler versions and the CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 3800X) in results/2026-10-05-kostya-ms7c37.js. The same algorithm runs on both sides and the lead holds in all five monthly runs checked, so the record's 'no stated mechanism' cap is not a tier rule.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 2026-10-05 run, CLBG::Fannkuchredux runtime in s: V/Clang 0.875 vs C/Gcc 1.036 (best of all gcc and clang C/C++ rows), about 1.18x faster (derived from page data); C/Clang 1.174 (1.34x); C++/Clang++ 1.128; C++/G++ 1.199. Against the -O3 -march=native rows: best -O3 C/C++ row C++/Clang++/Unsafe 1.137 (1.30x), C/Clang/Fast 1.278, C/Gcc/Fast 1.364. Flag-matched pair: V/Clang/Perf (clang -O3 -march=native -flto) 0.912 vs C/Clang/Fast (clang -O3 -march=native) 1.278, about 1.40x (derived). With the GCC backend V loses: V/GCC 1.126 vs C/Gcc 1.036 (about 1.09x slower) and V/GCC/Perf 1.08. Stable in five monthly runs (2026-07-14, 08-14, 09-03, 09-18, 10-05): V/Clang 0.862-0.879 s vs the best gcc or clang C/C++ row, always C/Gcc, at 1.020-1.047 s (1.18-1.20x, derived); V/GCC 1.122-1.133 s, slower than C/Gcc in every run.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: V 0.5.1 (0c3183c) 'v -enable-globals -cc clang -prod' with clang 22.1.8; V emits C, and -prod adds -O3 and -flto to the C compiler call (v3_prod_c_optimization_flags in vlang/v master vlib/v/driver/driver.v, -O2 only for very large generated units; the 0.5.1 builder itself was not checked), no -march=native. V/Clang/Perf and V/GCC/Perf add -cflags '-O3 -march=native -flto'. C/C++ rows: GCC 16.0.1 20260322 (trunk r16-8246, Ubuntu build) and Clang 22.1.8. 'prod' (c/Makefile CFLAGS_PROD, cpp/Makefile CXXFLAGS_PROD): -O2 -DNDEBUG -fstack-protector-strong -fno-omit-frame-pointer, linked with -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now -Wl,--gc-sections. 'Fast': -O3 -march=native -mtune=native -DNDEBUG -pipe -fstack-protector -ftree-vectorize -funroll-loops, with -flto=thin passed only at link time. 'Unsafe': -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG -pipe -fno-stack-protector -fomit-frame-pointer -ffast-math -fvisibility=hidden -fno-common -fstrict-overflow -fno-trapping-math, with -flto=full only at link time. Because the LTO flags appear only in LDFLAGS, the Fast and Unsafe builds probably get no real LTO (inference from the Makefiles). PGO rows are -O2 plus profile use.
corrections.workload: CLBG fannkuch-redux with n = 8 (8! = 40,320 permutations per call), 700 iterations, checksum 135762480 verified by the suite (run.js); permutation arrays sized 32 ints. Same algorithm in every language: count-array permutation generator, prefix reversal by swaps, checksum and max-flips. Runtime of the benchmark in seconds.
corrections.why_faster: Not a V language mechanism. V compiles to C, and the V/Clang row is V-generated C put through the same clang 22.1.8 at -O3 -flto. The two sources differ only in shape: the hand-written C copies each permutation with a runtime-length memcpy(perm, perm1, n*sizeof(int)) and swaps through a static pointer helper, while the V source copies with an element loop and swaps inline. The gap is clang-specific (V through gcc is slower than C through gcc in all five runs), so it reflects how each compiler handles two equivalent C sources rather than anything V adds; no profile or disassembly is published to pin it down.
corrections.caveats: V is a C transpiler, so this is V-generated C against hand-written C, both compiled by clang or gcc; the win appears only with clang (V/Clang 0.875 s vs C/Clang 1.174 s) and reverses with gcc (V/GCC 1.126 s vs C/Gcc 1.036 s), which points to codegen differences between two equivalent C sources (runtime-length memcpy and a pointer swap helper in the C file, plain loops in V) rather than a language advantage. The headline C 'prod' rows are -O2 with hardening and V -prod is -O3 -flto, but the flag-matched V/Clang/Perf vs C/Clang/Fast pair (both clang -O3 -march=native) still shows 1.40x; note that on this test every -O3 -march=native C/C++ row is slower than the -O2 C/Gcc row, so the -O3 rows are not the strongest C baseline. One benchmark only: V is slower than C elsewhere in the same file (Nbody 1.86 s vs 1.465 s). Gossamer (0.913 s), Nim/Clang (0.918 s) and Zig (0.977 s) also beat the C rows here. Each configuration is timed once per monthly run; the lead is stable across five runs. LangArena's README calls it a subjective, not peer-reviewed suite whose translations were AI-assisted and reviewed by the author.

notes: Every number verified in the results files (2026-10-05 plus four earlier monthly runs); metadata confirmed (MIT, 41 stars, last commit 2026-10-08, not a fork). Tier raised C to A on the LangArena precedent; same_opt_level set true via the flag-matched V/Clang/Perf vs C/Clang/Fast pair. Shortcomings to record: clang-only win that reverses under gcc (V/GCC 1.09x slower than C/Gcc), V emits C so the gap is source-shape codegen not a language mechanism, single benchmark, -O3 C rows slower than -O2 on this test.

tier_reason: Upgraded C to A on the LangArena precedent (Zig Etc::Words and Distance::NGram entries in this wave): public code for every side (zig/src/fannkuchredux.zig, c/src/fannkuchredux.c, cpp/src/fannkuchredux.cpp; workload in run.js), build modes in zig/build.zig, flags in c/Makefile and cpp/Makefile, versions, build commands and the CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 3800X) in results/2026-10-05-kostya-ms7c37.js. The margin is small (1.04-1.07x over the best C row) but present in all five monthly runs checked.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 2026-10-05 run, CLBG::Fannkuchredux runtime in s: Zig (ReleaseSafe) 0.977 vs C/Gcc 1.036 (best of all gcc and clang C/C++ rows), about 1.06x faster (derived from page data); C/Clang 1.174 (1.20x). Against the -O3 -march=native rows: best -O3 C/C++ row C++/Clang++/Unsafe 1.137 (1.16x), C/Clang/Fast 1.278 (1.31x), C/Gcc/Fast 1.364. Zig/Unchecked (ReleaseFast) is slower than the safe build at 1.024 s. Five monthly runs (2026-07-14 to 2026-10-05): Zig 0.972-0.989 s vs the best gcc or clang C/C++ row, always C/Gcc, at 1.020-1.047 s (1.04-1.07x, derived); Zig/Unchecked 1.024-1.054 s, slower than ReleaseSafe in every run. The suite author's own mycc C compiler (LLVM backend) reached 1.006 s on 2026-08-14, still behind Zig's 0.972 s that month.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zig 0.17.0 (0.16.0 in the July to September runs) 'zig build build-zig': zig/build.zig builds this row with optimize = .ReleaseSafe (LLVM release optimisation with runtime safety checks kept) and b.standardTargetOptions(.{}), which defaults to the native host CPU, so it is closer to -O3 -march=native with bounds checks than to the generic -O2 prod C build; Zig/Unchecked is the same source at .ReleaseFast. C/C++ rows: GCC 16.0.1 20260322 (trunk r16-8246, Ubuntu build) and Clang 22.1.8. 'prod' (c/Makefile CFLAGS_PROD, cpp/Makefile CXXFLAGS_PROD): -O2 -DNDEBUG -fstack-protector-strong -fno-omit-frame-pointer, linked with -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now -Wl,--gc-sections. 'Fast': -O3 -march=native -mtune=native -DNDEBUG -pipe -fstack-protector -ftree-vectorize -funroll-loops, with -flto=thin passed only at link time. 'Unsafe': -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG -pipe -fno-stack-protector -fomit-frame-pointer -ffast-math -fvisibility=hidden -fno-common -fstrict-overflow -fno-trapping-math, with -flto=full only at link time. Because the LTO flags appear only in LDFLAGS, the Fast and Unsafe builds probably get no real LTO (inference from the Makefiles). PGO rows are -O2 plus profile use.
corrections.workload: CLBG fannkuch-redux with n = 8 (8! = 40,320 permutations per call), 700 iterations, checksum 135762480 verified by the suite (run.js); permutation arrays sized 32 ints. Same algorithm in every language. Runtime of the benchmark in seconds.
corrections.why_faster: Not established and not a Zig language feature. Both sides run the same permutation and prefix-reversal loops; Zig differs in shape only (a two-index i<j swap loop instead of the C precomputed k2 count, @memcpy instead of memcpy, inline swap instead of a pointer helper) and keeps safety checks. The C -O3 -march=native rows are slower than the -O2 row, so CPU targeting does not explain it either; the small, stable margin reflects how LLVM (Zig) and gcc/clang (C) schedule two equivalent loops. The suite publishes no profile.
corrections.caveats: Small margin on one benchmark (1.04-1.07x over the best C row across five monthly runs), stable rather than noise, but from codegen differences between equivalent loops, not a Zig language mechanism. Zig/Unchecked (ReleaseFast) is consistently 3-8% slower than the safe ReleaseSafe build, a systematic codegen or layout effect that shows how sensitive this kernel is to compilation details. Zig's production row targets the native CPU (b.standardTargetOptions default) while the C prod rows are generic x86-64 -O2 with hardening, but the -O3 -march=native Fast and Unsafe C/C++ rows are slower (1.137-1.364 s), so flags do not explain the gap; on this test every -O3 C/C++ row is slower than the -O2 C/Gcc row. The Zig loop is written differently from the C loop (decrementing j against the C k2 count) and uses @memcpy. Zig is slower than C on Matmul and several other numeric rows in the same file. Each configuration is timed once per monthly run. LangArena's README calls it a subjective, not peer-reviewed suite whose translations were AI-assisted and reviewed by the author.

notes: Every number verified in the results files (2026-10-05 plus four earlier monthly runs); metadata confirmed (MIT, 41 stars, last commit 2026-10-08). Tier raised C to A on the LangArena precedent; same_opt_level set true because the -O3 -march=native C/C++ rows (flag-matched to Zig's native ReleaseSafe) also lose. Shortcomings to record: 1.04-1.07x margin on one benchmark, ReleaseFast slower than ReleaseSafe, codegen variance rather than a language mechanism, native-CPU Zig vs generic -O2 headline C row.

tier_reason: Every quoted number matches site/data/results/minima-sync.json and the sibling nginx, libreactorng, h2o, mongoose, libioma and drogon JSON files; the code is public (frameworks/minima-sync/{Dockerfile,minima-sync.csproj,Program.cs,io_uring/Native.cs,io_uring/Ring.cs}, frameworks/libreactorng/Dockerfile, frameworks/nginx/{Dockerfile,ngx_http_httparena_module.c}, scripts/benchmark.sh, scripts/lib/profiles.sh), flags are in the Dockerfiles and the CPU (Threadripper PRO 3995WX) in site/data/current.json, the HttpArena tier-A precedent (actix, dusty, libxev, kestrel, tokio-uring).

corrections.claimed_speedup: baseline-4096: 4,386,544 req/s vs nginx 3,284,513 (1.34x, derived from page data), h2o 3,641,609 (1.20x), mongoose 3,707,598 (1.18x), libioma 4,255,834 (1.03x), libreactorng 4,377,377 (1.00x, parity) and Drogon 2,022,710 (2.17x); the Zig io_uring entry zeemo is ahead at 4,422,489 and libxev (Zig) ties at 4,381,919, all at the roughly 4.4M req/s baseline ceiling the suite itself names in scripts/lib/profiles.sh. pipelined-4096 (reference-only): 57,140,640 vs libreactorng 43,424,448 (1.32x), h2o 4,938,603 (11.6x), nginx 4,037,345 (14.2x); libioma and mongoose have no pipelined result. limited-conn-4096: 2,687,059 vs libioma 2,707,029 (0.99x), mongoose 2,701,933 (0.99x), libreactorng 2,685,717 (1.00x), h2o 2,651,569 (1.01x), nginx 2,626,297 (1.02x). Ordinary .NET servers in the same suite: Kestrel 1,320,795 and ASP.NET Core minimal 1,305,946 req/s at baseline-4096.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: C#: mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 image, 'dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64 -p:PublishAot=true' with clang and zlib1g-dev for the native link; csproj sets PublishAot, Optimize, ServerGarbageCollection, InvariantGlobalization and AllowUnsafeBlocks, and no IlcInstructionSet, so the binary targets generic x86-64. The io_uring bindings are C# (raw io_uring_setup/enter/register through libc syscall(), mmap'd rings), not liburing. C side: libreactorng at pinned commit 7a65f8b plus a connection-close patch, library configured with CFLAGS='-O3 -march=native' and server.c built with gcc -O3 -march=native (ubuntu:24.04 build-essential, compiler version not stated); nginx 1.31.4 with a custom handler module, --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG' (debian:trixie build-essential, version not stated); libioma and mongoose -O3 -march=native with LTO, h2o CMake Release with clang -march=native, Drogon handler only against the prebuilt drogonframework/drogon:latest image.
corrections.why_faster: No language mechanism. At baseline-4096 minima-sync ties the C io_uring entries (libreactorng 1.00x, libioma 1.03x) at the harness ceiling of about 4.4M req/s and trails the Zig zeemo entry. Its margins over nginx, h2o and mongoose come from architecture (a synchronous single-issuer io_uring reactor per pinned core with multishot accept, against epoll-based event loops) and from a minimal response with no Date or Server header (62.9 bytes per response vs 108.7 for libreactorng and 135.4 for nginx, derived from bandwidth divided by req/s). The pipelined lead over libreactorng (1.32x) also comes with 61.4 vs 106.2 bytes per response.
corrections.caveats: Parity, not a win, against the C server with the same design: 1.00x libreactorng at baseline-4096 and limited-conn-4096, below libioma and mongoose at limited-conn, and the top baseline entries (zeemo, minima-sync, libxev, libreactorng) sit within 4% at the roughly 4.4M req/s ceiling that scripts/lib/profiles.sh names, with the gcannon load generator pinned to the other half of the machine (CPUs 32-63,96-127). The gains over nginx (1.34x), h2o and mongoose compare a minimal io_uring server against epoll servers and different response sizes (62.9 bytes per response vs nginx 135.4, Drogon 134.4, libreactorng 108.7, libioma 85.8, mongoose 72.5; derived from bandwidth divided by req/s), so same_algorithm is false. The pipelined profile (16x batched) is reference-only in HttpArena's composite score. The contender was written by the suite owner MDA2AV (PR #824, 2026-06-07) and exists only inside the HttpArena repo (meta.json repo is empty), modelled on the Zig zeemo architecture; the same-owner ioxide entry was tiered C in this wave while suite-owner entries such as kestrel kept A. Results are best of 3 runs of 5 s each (RUNS=3 in scripts/lib/common.sh), not one run, but the JSON files are undated and rows come from different runs on the same machine: minima-sync.json was last re-measured on or before 2026-08-29 (later commits only dropped profiles), libreactorng.json on 2026-09-07 and nginx.json in August. C/C++ entries are built -O3 -march=native (libioma and mongoose with LTO) or CMake Release with clang -march=native (h2o), while the C# binary targets generic x86-64, so the flags favour the C side; Drogon compiles only its handler against the prebuilt drogonframework/drogon:latest image, so the Drogon ratios are weaker evidence. The C competitor handlers are minimal hand-written servers by the suite maintainers or contributors, not tuned production configurations. The ordinary .NET servers are far slower than nginx at baseline-4096 (Kestrel 1,320,795 req/s).

notes: All numbers verified against the HttpArena JSON files; metadata confirmed (MIT, 128 stars, last commit 2026-10-11, not a fork). Tier A kept on the HttpArena precedent. Corrected: same_algorithm false, runs are best of 3 not one, compiler details. Shortcomings to record: parity with libreactorng (C) at the harness's 4.4M req/s ceiling and behind libioma and mongoose on limited-conn; wins only over epoll servers with larger responses or on the reference-only pipelined profile; contender written by the suite owner (ioxide precedent was C); cross-run rows.
